table.ruleA: Add the cycle's input row to each stage; rated charge not enforced.
table.ruleB: Add the cycle's inflow row to each tank; volume not enforced.

table.ruleA: Stages 1 to 6 in order, one at a time. If charge > rated (strict), excess goes to stage n+1 (already there when n+1 is handled, so it can cascade) and the stage is set to rated. Stage 6 excess goes to ground.
table.ruleB: Tanks 1 to 6 in order, one at a time. If contents > volume (strict), excess goes to tank n+1 (already there when n+1 is handled, so it can cascade) and the tank is set to volume. Tank 6 excess goes to outfall.

table.ruleA: Read charge after Step 2. CLEAR and charge >= upper mark: ASSERTED. ASSERTED and charge <= lower mark: CLEAR. Otherwise no change. Log (cycle, stage, before, after); at most one change per cycle.
table.ruleB: Read contents after Step 2. STEADY and contents >= upper mark: OVERLOADED. OVERLOADED and contents <= lower mark: STEADY. Otherwise no change. Log (cycle, tank, before, after); at most one change per cycle.

table.ruleA: All six amounts are worked out first from the charge at the start of the step, using the state after Step 3. CLEAR: floor(charge/4), goes to ground. ASSERTED: floor(charge/2), goes to stage n-1 (stage 1's goes to ground). All applied at once; no rated cap.
table.ruleB: All six amounts are worked out first from the contents at the start of the step, using the state after Step 3. STEADY: floor(contents/4), goes to outfall. OVERLOADED: floor(contents/2), goes to tank n-1 (tank 1's goes to outfall). All applied at once; no volume cap.

table.ruleA: If the sum of all six charges > 38 (strict; 38 does not trip), EVERY stage becomes floor(charge/2). The removed charge goes to ground. Log the cycle.
table.ruleB: If the sum of all six contents > 38 (strict; 38 does not trip), only OVERLOADED tanks become floor(contents/2). STEADY tanks are left unchanged. The removed liquor goes to outfall. Log the cycle.
table.difference: Which positions the halving applies to. A halves all six positions. B halves only positions in the high state (OVERLOADED = ASSERTED). A low-state position holding 2 or more units at a halving cycle keeps its contents in B but loses half in A. This changes end quantities and the loss tally, and through later cycles it can change states, state changes and later halving cycles.

table.ruleA: (a) end charges 1-6, (b) end states, (c) state changes in order, (d) breaker-trip cycles, (e) ground total, (f) balance check: start + inputs = end + ground.
table.ruleB: (a) end contents 1-6, (b) end states, (c) state changes, (d) storm-bypass cycles, (e) outfall total, (f) balance check: start + inflows = end + outfall.

result.probeWhy: The probe is built so the halving fires in cycle 1 while a low-state position holds a lot. Stage 1 starts at 6, just under its upper mark of 7, and gets no input, so it stays CLEAR/STEADY. Stages 2 to 6 go over their upper marks, become high-state, and return half of their charge upstream. Stage 1 then ends Step 4 at 9 (6 - 1 + 4), and the line total is 42 > 38. A halves stage 1 to 4. B leaves it at 9. Hand check of cycle 1: after Step 2 the charges are [6,8,9,6,7,7] (ground 1). After Step 4 they are [9,8,8,6,7,4] (ground 2). A gives [4,4,4,3,3,2] with ground 24. B gives [9,4,4,3,3,2] with ground 19. The printed tables never trip this. At their halving cycles (1 and 4) every low-state position holds 0 or 1, and halving 0 or 1 gives the same result as leaving it, so the two rules agree on the printed data. Balance checks: printed 114 = end + loss for both; probe 44 = 15+29 (A) = 14+30 (B).
result.differingRule: In Step 5, when the line total is over 38, A halves every position, but B halves only positions in the high state (OVERLOADED) and leaves STEADY ones unchanged.
result.trust: Both routes agree on DIFFERENT and on which rule causes it. On their own printed tables the two documents give identical reports: halving in cycles 1 and 4, loss 76, ends [6,10,9,7,4,2]. That is because at each halving cycle every low-state position holds 0 or 1 unit. The difference only shows when a low-state position holds 2 or more units at a halving cycle, and the probe is built to do that. The arithmetic was done with a Python script, C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P15\sim.py, and the probe runs are in probe.py in the same folder. I checked cycle 1 of the probe by hand. A random search over 20,000 tables (search.py) found a difference in about 16% of them. A probe I tried earlier, with start all 9s, did not separate the two, which shows a probe has to be aimed at this case.

differing_rule_truth: DIFF (hidden on frozen data): step 5 halves only ELEVATED cells
